summary: Orna Almogi specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Ngagyur Nyingma Institute and under Khenpo Wangchuk Sonam, David P. Jackson, and Lambert Schmithausen. She held posts at the Nepal-German Manuscript Preservation Project and the University of Hamburg (attested 2004–2007).

Osamu Hayashima is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology who studied under Noritoshi Aramaki and at the University of Hamburg (1992). He held posts at Nagasaki University (attested 1979–1984; 1995–2003), Shiga University of Medical Science (attested 2003–2013), and Ryukoku University (attested 2013–2015).
Osamu Izumoji works in the fields of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He has held academic posts at Kyoto Prefectural University and Ryukoku University.

Osamu Oba was a scholar of Sinology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Kansai University (~1950–1953) and later held posts at Kansai University (~1968–1998), Kogakkan University (~1998–2002), and the University of the Sacred Heart.

Osamu Takata was a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology who studied under Baiei Henmi. He held positions at Tohoku University (attested 1961) and the Tokyo National Research Institute for Cultural Properties (attested 1967).

Osborn Bergin was a linguist who studied at University College Cork, the School of Irish Learning, and the University of Freiburg, studying under Heinrich Zimmer and Kuno Meyer. He held posts at University College Dublin (~1909–1940) and Dublin Institute for Advanced Studies (~1940–1950).

Oskar von Hinüber is an Indologist, Buddhist studies scholar, and linguist who studied at Mainz, Tübingen, and Erlangen-Nürnberg under Paul Thieme. He held posts at Mainz (1965–1981), the Nepal Research Centre (~1971–1972), and the Chair in Indic Studies at Freiburg (1981–2006).

Osmund Bopearachchi studied at the University of Kelaniya, CNRS, Panthéon-Sorbonne University, and Paris-Sorbonne University. He held positions at CNRS (from 1989) and as Adjunct Professor at the University of California, Berkeley (~2014).

Osvald Sirén was an art historian and sinologist who studied at the University of Helsinki. He held posts at the University of Stockholm (1908–1923), Harvard and Yale (1916–1917), the Musée Guimet (1924–1925), and the Nationalmuseum (1926–1945).

Othmar Frank studied at the University of Paris and in London. He held teaching posts at Banz Abbey School, Kaiser-Heinrich-Gymnasium Bamberg, and professorships at the universities of Bamberg (~1807), Würzburg (1821), and Munich (1826).
Otoya Tanaka was an Indologist who studied at the University of Tokyo under Naoshiro Tsuji (~1927–1930). He later held a professorship at Chuo University (~1950–1974).
Otto Blau studied at the University of Leipzig (~1847–1848) and the University of Halle / Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1848–1852), where he studied under August Friedrich Pott.

Otto Fischer was a scholar of Sinology, Japanology, and history/archaeology. He studied at Tübingen, Munich, Vienna, and Göttingen, and held positions as director at the Staatsgalerie Stuttgart (1920) and Kunstmuseum Basel (1927), and professor at the University of Basel (~1927–1937).

Otto Franke was a scholar of Sinology, Indology, and Buddhist studies who studied at Freiburg, Göttingen, and under Wilhelm Grube. He held chairs at the Hamburg Colonial Institute/University of Hamburg (1910–1923) and the University of Berlin (1923–1931).

Otto Höfler was a scholar of linguistics and history who studied at Vienna, Lund, and Kiel, including under Rudolf Much. He held posts at Uppsala (1928–1934), Kiel (1935), Munich (1938–1945, 1954), and the University of Vienna (1957–1971).

Otto Jahn was an archaeologist, historian, and philologist who studied at Kiel, Leipzig, and Berlin. He held posts at Kiel University (~1839–1842), the University of Greifswald (~1842–1847), the University of Leipzig (~1847–1851), and the University of Bonn (~1855–1869).

Otto Maenchen-Helfen was a historian, Sinologist, and Central Asian scholar who studied at Vienna, Gothenburg, and Leipzig under August Conrady. He held posts at the Marx-Engels-Lenin Institute (1927–1929), Mills College (1939–1947), and UC Berkeley (1947–1962).

Otto Neugebauer was a historian of mathematics and science who studied at Graz, Munich, and Göttingen under Boris Turayev. He held positions at Göttingen (1923–1933), Copenhagen (1933–1939), Brown University (1939–1969), and the Institute for Advanced Study (1950, 1980–1990).

Otto Rosenberg was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Saint Petersburg and Bonn under Theodore Stcherbatsky, Sergey Oldenburg, and Rudolf Lange, and held a post at the University of Saint Petersburg (1911–1919).

Otto Stein was an Indologist who studied at the German University of Prague under Moriz Winternitz and Heinrich Swoboda (1912–1918). In 1929, he became a member of the research section at the Oriental Institute of the Czech Academy of Sciences.
